newsitem.title: USA: US spot prods drop at close, gasoline diffs suffer.
newsitem.headline: US spot prods drop at close, gasoline diffs suffer.

text.p: U.S. spot product prices weakened Friday afternoon, led by the dip in gasoline differentials and pullback on the NYMEX.
NYMEX heating oil and gasoline futures prices dipped slightly toward the close, extending the drop seen during the previous trading session.

Weakness in the gasoline diffs appeared to be tied to concerns about large imports reported to be headed to the U.S. East Coast. As many as 25 tankers have been fixed over the last week to carry about 8.5 million barrels to the U.S., according to European traders.
In New York Harbor (NYH), prompt unleaded conventional M5 barrels were talked between 2.00 and 2.25 cents under the screen, down about 0.25 cent on the day.
U.S. Gulf (USG) conventional unleaded for delivery on the Colonial Pipeline's back 1st cycle was offered at 2.80 cents under the print, down more than 0.50 cent from Thursday.

Prompt No. 2 oil diffs at NYH remained steady, hovering near a 0.50 premium to the NYMEX, while USG No. 2 for the back 1st Colonial cycle was offered at 4.40 cents under, up slightly on the day in very thin activity, according to players.
-- Matt Daily, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1626
